In this summer heat I'm sure a lot of you are relying on those trusty airmovers to get some relieve.

Fans tend to collect dust and grease, just a small buildup on the leading edge of a fanblade greatly reduces its effectiveness. Simply wipe it down and clean it of any grease, most standing fans can be taken apart easily (disconnect it tho first please), clean the cage and the fanblades and you will get a much nicer flow of air.
LPT: Clean your fanblades to get more air from your fan and use less electricity.

Little something I picked up as well. It is a good practice to wipe from the inner part of the blade (where it attaches) to the end. This is so that you don't accidently wipe the dust into the motor.

Just something that others might not consider.

SSDs have been decreasing in price per gigabyte for years, and people have long been predicting when they'd replace HDDs. But the problem is HDDs keep getting cheaper and bigger storage-wise too. I personally feel like HDDs are and outdated technology and SSDs should be the successor to hard drives, not an alternative.

Will we ever see price parity between the two, or will they always be at odds?

Side note: I know it's not typical to post these kinds of posts on Reddit's technology subreddit, but it seems that's mostly because a culture of content has developed there which now determines what sort of post is considered typical. I've noticed a lot these sorts of posts don't really have a place on Reddit, so I'm wondering if Voat can change that; where should be the place for open ended, sort of speculative questions and discussions on certain topics? I feel like there is a void of this sort of content on any high-profile areas of Reddit.
Will SSDs ever see price-parity with HDDs, or are we doomed to forever choose between slow, clunky high-capacity and fast, sleek lower-capacity (also quick meta-discussion)?

My guess is that within the next 5 years we will see SSD's at the same price per GB ratio as consumer HDDs, then a few years later be significantly cheaper than HDDs. For example, when 1TB SSDs were coming out, they cost around a thousand dollars, now, you can get a Samsung 850 EVO 1TB for around four hundred dollars.

At some point, there will be little difference, then the older tech will finally die. Even current storage tech will need to change in order to meet the ever increasing needs for storage. Since Samsung just rolled out a 2 TB SSD for ~$800, I would guess within the next 5 years or so.
